criteria.evidence: "## What it does" "## Inputs / Outputs" "## Rules & behavior" "## Acceptance criteria" "## Out of scope" "## Agent intent (ICE)" "Out: when Phoenix memory cannot be reached, a plain message that says so and that the Phoenix install must run on this machine, and no memory built."

"It never writes Phoenix memory and never writes another project's memory, because Phoenix memory is shared by every project on the machine and a write there from one project would change what the others draw from." "The reply is per part because one changed standard can be welcome and another in the same block not, and a yes for the whole block only would force the product owner to take both." "An empty answer there would look like "no block fits" and leave the project with too little memory."

"Phoenix memory (a word this page uses) is the one shared memory on a machine" "Garura memory (a word this page uses): a project's Garura memory is the project's own memory" "A yes to an added part builds it into the project's Garura memory and adds it, with its place in Phoenix memory and its fingerprint, to the block list." "Given a brief that names two changed parts in the database block, when the product owner types yes to the first and no to the second, then"

"A part the list holds whose fingerprint differs is changed. A part the selection now finds that the list does not hold is added. A part the list holds that the selection no longer finds is taken out." "For each block it holds the answer that selected it, the block's selection, for each part the block was built from its place in Phoenix memory (the file and the part of it) and its fingerprint"

"Memory reaches a project in three steps, and this feature is the third." "It keeps each project's blocks its own. A person installs Phoenix once on a machine and initializes many projects there, each with different answers, so two projects hold different blocks taken from the one Phoenix memory" "Adding or taking out a whole block when an answer changes: Run initialize again (fn-rerun-initialize) owns it."

prior.evidence: "Phoenix memory (a word this page uses) is the one shared memory on a machine (the domain shelves, the standards, the templates) that every project on that machine draws from." "A memory block (a word this page uses) is the relevant part of Phoenix memory that one setup answer selects" "Where these words come from: the sources say what a block holds" "What a yes is given to: the brief lists each changed, added or taken-out part under its block and asks for a yes or no to each part;" "A yes to a changed part rebuilds what the project's Garura memory holds for that part from what Phoenix memory holds now" "A yes to a taken-out part removes what the project's memory built from it and takes it out of the block list" "A no to any of the three leaves that part and its block-list entry as they were"
